messages:
acme_ops: Hey team, starting ~2026-03-14 08:12 UTC our service consuming streaming JSON from Redwood started throwing JSONDecodeError mid-stream. Happens only in production behind ALB. Python SDK consumers hit an exception parsing an incomplete unicode escape (\\uXXXX) at a chunk boundary.

acme_ops: Example traceback: `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Invalid \uXXXX escape` (line in our consumer). We only see this with stream=True. No obvious payload corruption on our side.

sarah_support: Sorry for the trouble — can you share a minimal repro snippet, SDK version, and whether any proxies/gzip/alt-codings are in place? Also rough timing of when it started.

acme_ops: Repro (very small):
```python
# py 3.10, redwood-python 0.4.2
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., streaming=True)
resp = client.generate_stream(model="x-small", prompt="say hi")
for chunk in resp:
    # our parser expects JSON objects per event
    obj = json.loads(chunk)  # sometimes fails here
```
We captured raw chunks around failure. Sequence (line-delimited chunks):
```
data: {"event":"out","payload":"{\\\"text\\\":\\\"hello \\\\\\\u"}
```
next chunk:
```
data: 00\\\"}\\n"
```
Combined that yields `...\\u00\"` which is an invalid/incomplete escape.

jordan_dev: Thanks, that raw capture is super helpful. A few Qs:
- Is ALB doing any buffering or chunk coalescing?
- Any auth refresh/401->retry behavior around the same timestamp?
- Are you using gzip/transfer-encoding modifications?

acme_ops: ALB in front, no gzip (we verified Content-Encoding absent). We did see a spike of 401->refresh attempts around the same minute (token refresher retried once). No middleware that touches body.

bina_eng: This looks like a streaming framing edge we recently shipped a guard for but not backported to 0.4.2. Reproduction notes: if a retry/heartbeat injects a very small chunk boundary right inside a JSON string unicode escape (e.g., "\\u00" split across chunks) some streaming consumers that treat each chunk as an independent JSON payload will attempt to parse prematurely and fail.

bina_eng: Short-term workarounds:
- upgrade redwood-python to 0.4.3 (contains the streaming-buffer fix)
- or buffer bytes until you see a complete JSON object (e.g., wait for matching braces) before calling json.loads
- or disable streaming on client side (stream=False) if acceptable.

bina_eng: We will push a staged fix to runtime and ship SDK 0.4.3 with a new flag `streaming_json_buffer=True` that buffers incomplete chunks until a full JSON object is assembled.

acme_ops: Thanks — we tested 0.4.3 on staging and the consumer no longer throws. Go client in our infra still hit a rare desync when using http2 multiplexing; we'll send a minimal capture.

deploy_bot: Patch release redwood-runtime@2026-03-18T02:00Z scheduled for staging (includes streaming framing guard).

sarah_support: Marking this as high priority until Go flakiness is resolved. Jordan and Bina assigned to investigate Go http2 framing interplay. @acme_ops can you open another thread with the Go capture if it reoccurs?

acme_ops: Will do. For now 0.4.3 + staging runtime looks good; thanks for the quick turnaround.

sarah_support: Great — closing this thread once you confirm production stability in 24h. :thumbsup:
